paper.title: Continual Harness: Online Adaptation for Self-Improving Foundation Agents
paper.central_claim: A reset-free self-improving harness: starting from a minimal environment interface, an automated Refiner rewrites the agent's prompt, sub-agents, skills and memory mid-episode, substantially reducing button-press cost on Pokemon Red/Emerald and recovering a majority of the gap to a hand-engineered expert harness, and an online model-harness co-learning loop yields sustained milestone progress in an open-source model.

signatures.object: Harness state H = (system prompt, sub-agents, skills incl. executable code, memory) of a frozen foundation-model agent; baseline = minimal harness with generic prompt and no sub-agents, memory or skills.
signatures.information: Refiner (same model as the agent) reads the recent trajectory window and the harness; sees frames/text map/actions/tool logs; no walkthrough, milestone schedule or decompilation. Agent and Refiner share a meta-tool API.
signatures.operation: Every F steps after warm-up W: identify failure signatures -> four passes (rewrite prompt; create/edit/delete sub-agents; codify/repair skills; add/update/demote memories) -> apply edits in place.
signatures.output: Updated harness state used from the next step; no episode reset.
signatures.conditions: F and W values and Refiner prompts not given in the text; Pokemon Red and Emerald; Gemini 3 Pro/Flash/Flash-Lite.
signatures.feedback: Trajectory evidence (navigation loops, tool failures, stalls); environment milestones are the evaluation metric.
signatures.selection_rule: None: edits are applied directly; unused entries removed by Refiner judgment; no held-out gate or rollback.
signatures.persistence: Harness persists through the episode; the final harness of a successful run can be loaded as bootstrap (frozen or continuing).
signatures.later_use: Agent reads prompt, sub-agent and skill calls each step; memory catalog is listed in the prompt and pulled on demand.
signatures.claimed_effect: Fewer button presses/dollars to milestones; Pro on Emerald $130 vs $215; recovers a majority of the gap to expert harness (figure).
signatures.failure_boundary: Capability floor (Flash-Lite below minimal); Red bootstrap-updating regression; create-and-forget tail; rarely pulled memory.

signatures.object: Open-source policy weights (Gemma-4) trained inside the refining harness; the harness state co-adapts. Weight-updating component, outside the non-weight scope but coupled to it.
signatures.information: Pairwise PRM (Gemini-3-flash-preview) scores transitions; Gemini-3.1-pro relabels low-reward windows.
signatures.operation: 256-step reset-free DAgger rollout through the live harness -> PRM scoring -> teacher relabel -> soft SFT -> next iteration from saved emulator state.
signatures.conditions: SFT and offline GRPO warm-ups produce no milestone advancement alone; Red only.
signatures.selection_data: Same game and rollouts that are reported.
signatures.persistence: Weights and emulator state across iterations.
signatures.claimed_effect: Milestone index rises across iterations in five advancing runs from beginning and mid-game checkpoints.
signatures.failure_boundary: Non-monotonic reward, bursty advances, resume regression; no run where weights alone, harness alone or no teacher is compared.

gap.author_gap: Coding harnesses exist but not for long-horizon partially observable embodied decision making, and prompt-optimisation methods need episode resets, so harness refinement cannot proceed mid-episode.
gap.checked_gap: A real, specific limitation: reset-based optimisers cannot reach late-episode failures and resets are costly; supported by the PokeAgent Challenge result that unscaffolded VLMs make little progress. The claimed advantage of reset-free refinement over reset-based optimisation is argued by construction and never tested head-to-head.
gap.lineage: Coding harnesses (Claude Code, OpenHands) -> PokeAgent Challenge with hand-designed expert harness -> GPP human-in-the-loop refinement and agent-built meta-tools -> Continual Harness (automated Refiner, reset-free). Neighbours: GEPA-style prompt optimisation, reflective self-improvement, Voyager-like tool building, in-context RL.
gap.closest_adjacent: GEPA / prompt-optimisation and reflection methods are cited and described but not run; Voyager-style self-built skills overlap with the 'meta-harness' operating point of the later GPP runs.
gap.residue: Whether refinement or the added meta-tools/memory/code execution produces the gain, how it compares with episodic optimisation, and what gate would stop regressions.
gap.stakes: Long-horizon embodied agents where free resets are unavailable and per-run cost matters.
gap.method_response: LLM Refiner edits all four harness components in place from trajectory windows; optionally transfers via bootstrap; optionally co-trains weights.
gap.remaining_gap: Admission gate and rollback, capability floor, sub-agent selection prior, other games/domains.
unresolved: GEPA and Voyager full texts not fixed in this batch; novelty relative to them taken from the paper's characterisation.

claims.text: Continual Harness from scratch lowers cost to milestones vs the minimal harness and recovers a majority of the gap to the expert harness.
claims.setting: Pokemon Red (11 milestones to Thunder Badge) and Emerald (9 milestones to Knuckle Badge in Fig 5; 31 in Fig 6); Gemini 3 Pro/Flash/Flash-Lite; at least 3 seeds.
claims.baseline_control: Minimal harness (no meta-tools/memory), expert harness, bootstrap variants; no reset-based optimiser or Refiner-off meta-tools control.
claims.selection_vs_test: Online learning within the evaluated episode; same game.
claims.result: Pro/Emerald: 100% at $130 vs 98% at $215; Flash high variance (80% at $42 vs 77% at $30); Flash-Lite 3-13% vs 20%. 'Majority of gap' is read from a figure.
claims.allowed_conclusion: On Pro, automated refinement lowers cost on Emerald/Red relative to the minimal harness (author-reported, medians of >=3 seeds); the gain is capability-dependent and absent below Pro; attribution to refinement vs added tools is not isolated.

claims.text: Reset-free bootstrap transfer: a refined harness accelerates later runs and continued refinement adds value.
claims.setting: Bootstrap frozen vs updating, same game.
claims.result: Emerald bootstrap tracks from-scratch; Red bootstrap-updating better at every milestone per main text but drifts below from-scratch and minimal per appendix.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Inherited harness is used on Emerald; on Red continued refinement can regress when new unrepaired sub-agents displace inherited ones.

claims.text: Skills measurably self-improve toward an oracle within a reset-free run.
claims.setting: Warp-to-warp navigation, path-cost deficit vs BFS/Dijkstra reference.
claims.baseline_control: Minimal harness never invokes a navigation skill.
claims.result: Deficit falls from near-half-cost to single digits.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Descriptive evidence of in-run skill repair; contribution of the skill library to end-task gains not ablated.

claims.text: Online co-learning with a refining harness gives sustained milestone progress in an open-source model.
claims.setting: Gemma-4, Red, reset-free DAgger+PRM with Gemini-3.1-pro teacher.
claims.selection_vs_test: Same game; progress is the reported metric.
claims.result: Five advancing runs with differing configurations; bursty advances.
claims.allowed_conclusion: A teacher-assisted weight-updating loop moves a Gemma-4 policy forward in Red in selected runs; not attributable to the harness or to reset-free operation.

claims.text: GPP is the first AI system to complete multiple Pokemon RPGs.
claims.setting: Human-in-the-loop harness refinement, plus agent-built meta-tools in later runs.
claims.result: Completion record; many lifetime retries in Yellow Legacy Elite Four.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Context for the automation motivation, not evidence for the automated method.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With Gemini 3 Pro, an LLM Refiner that edits prompt, sub-agents, skills and memory in place during a single Pokemon run lowers cost to milestones relative to a minimal harness (Emerald $130 vs $215 median at full completion), with benefits that vanish below the capability floor; the inherited harness is reused on Emerald while Red shows a documented regression. The co-learning claim is supported only as sustained progress in selected Gemma-4 runs with a teacher.
assessment.not_supported: Advantage over reset-based optimisation; that refinement rather than added meta-tools/memory causes the gains; the 'majority of the gap' as a number; that co-learning works through the harness; generality beyond Pokemon.
unresolved: F and W values and Refiner prompts
Opus: CH vs H_min confounds the Refiner with agent-held meta-tools (opus:O06).
Opus: bootstrap spend is not amortised over the selected source run (opus:O07).
Opus (paper fact): Appendix E addresses LLM readers ('please focus on sections 1-6', opus:O08); treated as data, and the whole appendix was used.

G.reason: Opus sides with son55. The bottleneck is specific and sourced (unscaffolded VLMs stall on RPGs; episodic optimisers such as GEPA need resets). But the premise 'no equivalent exists for embodied agents' is contradicted by the paper's own related work, which names game agents that build their own tooling during play (opus:O02). The closest neighbour, the GPP meta-harness in which the agent edits its own harness via meta-tools, is described but not bounded as a residual. Anchor 2.

M.reason: Opus sides with son55. The mechanism is concrete (every F steps, windowed failure-signature diagnosis, then four per-component CRUD passes). But how failure signatures are identified is unspecified, edits are applied unconditionally, and the claim that refinement quality compounds with episode length is contradicted by the documented Red regression. No distinguishing prediction separates the Refiner from the agent-side meta-tools it shares (opus:O06). Key assumptions remain weak: anchor 2 (cf. r17b Bian Que, M=2 for an unspecified attribution step).

X.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Harness components and the edit API are explicit. F, W and the Refiner prompts are absent. There is no admission gate, versioning, rollback or conflict handling. Retirement is an LLM heuristic. Most memories and skills are never used. The co-learning initial policy (opus:O03) and the Red milestone indexing (opus:O04, O05) are internally inconsistent.

E.measurement.reason: Opus sides with son55. The headline outcomes are the standardised PokeAgent milestone sequence read from the emulator, cumulative button presses and dollar spend: objective and hard to game. sol's concerns are real but confined to the secondary skill claim (top-10% skill subset, a 'no re-update within 5 steps' success proxy) and to the co-learning judge and PRM. Not 4: the headline 'majority of the gap' is figure-only and Refiner spend inclusion is unstated.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Minimal/expert/refined and bootstrap frozen-vs-updating arms, capability scaling and mechanism traces exist. Missing: a Refiner-off meta-tools arm (opus:O06), a reset-based optimiser, component removals (the skills claim is made by inspection), and harness-off or teacher-off co-learning arms. The Red bootstrap result is internally inconsistent.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Online adaptation within the evaluated episode is the declared claim, run on two games with seeds. Bootstrap transfer is within the same game from a selected successful run. Co-learning shows selected runs on one game. There is no cross-game test and no walkthrough/pretraining contamination discussion.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 2 (A2 tier 2): at least three seeds with per-seed traces and inheritance mean±SD, plus honest negative and high-variance cells. No intervals or tests. Figure 7 shows only the five advancing co-learning runs out of an unstated total.

E.cost.reason: Opus sides with sol. The Emerald cost–completion Pareto in dollars per seed is a real cost comparison and includes an honest capability-floor negative. It falls short of 3: whether Refiner calls are in the spend is unstated, and the bootstrap variants' spend excludes the selected from-scratch run whose library they load (opus:O07). Red cost is not reported. The co-learning loop, a headline contribution, has no GPU, teacher or PRM cost at all.
